title: Enchiladas Suizas
subtitle: Chicken enchiladas in a creamy green chilli and crème fraîche sauce
excerpt: Shredded chicken rolled in corn tortillas, baked under a creamy green chilli sauce enriched with crème fraîche and finished with mozzarella. Richer and milder than the red sauce versions.
sourceNotes: Enchiladas suizas ('Swiss-style enchiladas'): a Mexican restaurant dish said to have been created at Sanborn's in Mexico City in the early 20th century, where Swiss dairy traditions influenced the sour cream and cheese topping. The version here adapts the classic using crème fraîche and green peppers in place of tomatillos.

recipe.freezeNotes: The cream sauce doesn't freeze well; the cream can separate on reheating. Best made and eaten the same day.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 4 hours ahead, cover, and refrigerate. Bring to room temperature before baking.

glossaryTerms.definition: Spanish for 'Swiss', applied to this dish because of its cream and cheese topping, which reflects Swiss dairy-influenced cooking traditions brought to Mexico City in the early 20th century.

content.text: enchiladas are the cream-sauced version of the dish: corn tortillas filled with shredded chicken and baked under a smooth, tangy green chilli sauce enriched with crème fraîche. The sauce is milder than the red chilli version and the dairy rounds out the heat. It comes together in one pan after you've made the chicken.

items.prepNote: halved, seeds removed for mild heat

content.text: The sauce is built by grilling the peppers until charred, then blending them with the other ingredients. The crème fraîche goes in last, off the heat, so it doesn't split.
Season the chicken thighs with cumin and salt. Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through. Rest 5 minutes, then shred.
Place the green peppers and jalapeños cut-side down under a hot grill for 10-12 minutes until charred and soft. Set aside for 5 minutes, then remove the skins.

Blend the roasted peppers and jalapeños with the garlic, coriander, and stock until smooth. Pour into a saucepan and simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the crème fraîche. Season with salt. Don't boil after adding the crème fraîche.
Heat the oven to 190°C. Spread a ladleful of cream sauce across the base of a roasting dish.
Dip each corn tortilla in the warm cream sauce for 10 seconds. Fill with shredded chicken, roll tightly, and place seam-side down in the dish. Repeat with all the tortillas.

Pour the remaining cream sauce over the enchiladas. Tear the mozzarella over the top. Bake at 190°C for 20 minutes until the cheese melts and the sauce bubbles at the edges. Rest 5 minutes. Serve with soured cream and lime wedges.

items.symptom: Cream sauce splits and looks grainy
items.cause: Crème fraîche added to a sauce that was still too hot, or boiled after adding it
items.fix: Take the sauce off the heat before stirring in the crème fraîche. It can go back on a very low heat to warm through but should not boil.

items.cause: Not enough jalapeño, or seeds removed
items.fix: Add more jalapeño next time, or leave some seeds in for more heat. A squeeze of lime at the end also sharpens the flavour.

items.cause: Fresh mozzarella releases a lot of moisture
items.fix: Pat the mozzarella dry before tearing over the top. A mix of mozzarella and grated cheddar reduces the moisture.

items.cause: Not dipped in warm sauce before rolling
items.fix: The sauce dip is the critical step. Work while the sauce is warm; cool sauce won't soften the corn tortilla.

content.text: Enchiladas suizas became well-known at Sanborn's restaurants in Mexico City in the early 20th century. The 'Swiss' name comes from the soured cream and cheese topping, which reminded diners of Swiss dairy products. From Mexico City the dish spread into Mexican-American cooking in the US. Today it appears in Tex-Mex cookbooks alongside the more common red sauce version.
